content: असुर {%a.%} [असु-र <ls>Uṇ. 1. 42</ls>] .²1 Living, alive, spiritual. .²2 An epithet of the Supreme Spirit or Varuṇa. .²3 Incorporeal, super-human, divine. .{@-रः@} [According to <ls>Nir.</ls> अ सुरताः स्थानेषु न सुष्ठु रताः स्थानेषु चपला इत्यर्थः; or अस्ताः प्रच्याविता देवैः स्थानेभ्यः or from असु; असुः प्राणः तेन तद्वन्तो भवन्ति रो मत्वर्थे; or सोर्देवानसृजत तत्सुराणां सुरत्वम्, असोः असुरानसृजत तदसुराणामसुरत्वम्; सोः = प्रशस्तादात्मनः प्रदेशात्] .²1 An evil spirit, a demon; the chief of the evil spirits; वृकद्वरसो असुरस्य वीरान् <ls>Rv. 2. 30. 4</ls>. The <ls>Rām.</ls> thus accounts for the name:-- सुराप्रतिग्रहाद्देवाः सुरा इत्यभिविश्रुताः . अप्रतिग्रहणात्तस्या दैतेयाश्चासुरास्तथा .. [In the oldest parts of the Ṛgveda the term {%Asura%} is used for the Supreme Spirit and in the sense of ‘god’, ‘divine’; it was applied to several of the chief deities such as Indra, Agni, and especially Varuṇa. It afterwards acquired an entirely opposite meaning, and came to signify a demon or an enemy of the gods. The Brāhmaṇas state that Prajāpati created {%Asuras%} with the breath ({%Asu%}); particularly from the lower breath. The <ls>Vāyu P.</ls> says that Asuras were first produced as sons from Prajāpatiʼs groin; <ab>cf.</ab> also <ls>Nir.</ls> above]. .²2 A general name for the enemies of gods, Daityas and Dānavas, distinguished from Rākṣasas descended from Pulastya; कानीयसा एव देवा ज्यायसा असुराः <ls>Bṛ. Up. 1. 3. 1</ls>; <ls>Bg. 11. 22</ls>. .²3 A ghost or spectre. .²4 The sun (said to be from अस् to shine). .²5 An elephant. .²6 An epithet of Rāhu. .²7 A cloud. .²8 <ab>N.</ab> of a warrior tribe. .{@-रा@} .²1 Night. .²2 A zodiacal sign. .²3 A prostitute. .{@-री@} .²1 A female demon, wife of an Asura. .²2 <ab>N.</ab> of the plant Sinapis Racemosa Roxb. (<lang>Mar.</lang> <ns>काळी मोहरी</ns>).
